results.title: Synthetic study: smartphone use and anxiety symptoms among first-year undergraduates (cross-sectional)
results.abstract: This synthetic cross-sectional survey (N = 1200 first-year undergraduates) reports a moderate positive association between self-reported daily smartphone hours and anxiety symptoms (r = 0.31). The design is cross-sectional; no causal direction can be established. Limitations: self-report measures, single campus, and possible reverse causation.

results.title: Synthetic study: a two-wave panel on bedtime scrolling and anxious mood
results.abstract: This synthetic two-wave panel study (N = 430 students, four-week interval) finds bedtime scrolling predicts later anxious mood (beta = 0.18) but not the reverse path. Authors caution that effects are small and moderation by coping style was not tested.

results.title: Synthetic review: interventions reducing problematic smartphone use
results.abstract: This synthetic meta-analysis (k = 24 trials, mostly small) reports heterogeneous effects on wellbeing; authors conclude evidence for causality remains mixed and populations differ by culture and age.
